title: Adaptive burst allocator, proportional surge metering, and soft-tier failover
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Implement an adaptive burst allocation system for Dedicated fleets that (1) lets tenants request temporary capacity boosts with fair share and soft guarantees, (2) meters burst usage proportionally and produces predictable overage invoices, and (3) gracefully falls back to lower-cost/compatible model tiers when reserved capacity is saturated. This ticket covers the allocator algorithm, per-tenant surge credit pool semantics, rate-limiter integration, invoice attribution changes, operator controls (pause, drain, emergency-disable), and end-to-end QA/observability.

Motivation: Customers on Dedicated want predictable latency and throughput guarantees but also need headroom for transient spikes (e.g., product launches). We currently lack a tenant-friendly burst policy that: a) avoids noisy-neighbor amplification, b) produces explainable billing, and c) provides safe automatic degradation when capacity is constrained.

High-level design:
- Adaptive Burst Allocator: token-bucket+priority scoring per-tenant that consumes from a configurable surge credit pool. The allocator runs per-pool and produces allocation decisions within a 250ms control window to preserve latency SLOs.
- Proportional Surge Metering: meter bursts using a two-component model: committed throughput (covered by reserve) and transient excess (surge buckets). Overage is computed as amortized token-units against the tenant's surge credits; when negative, overages are recorded in the billing pipeline with an itemized breakdown.
- Soft-tier Failover: when a request cannot be fully allocated to the primary node family, the router can (policy-controlled) downgrade to a lower-cost compatible family (same model variant w/ different quantization) with transparent latency/cost metadata attached to the response. This is opt-in per-tenant.

Trade-offs and constraints:
- Allocator complexity vs. predictability: the scoring function favors simpler metrics (recent QPS, error rate, credit balance) to keep decisions auditable. We avoid per-request slow models to not impact runtime.
- Billing atomization: per-request billing provides accuracy but increases bill generation load. We amortize using 1-minute windows and store summary rows to minimize DB pressure.
- Safety: any automatic downgrade must preserve correctness; we implement a hard circuit-breaker to disable soft-tier failover for tenants marked high-security.

Deliverables: prototyped allocator service, rate-limiter hooks in runtime, billing pipeline changes (surge ledger + summarizer), console controls and metrics, operator runbook, rollout gating and canary plan.
acceptance_criteria: Allocator service accepts surge requests and returns allocation outcomes within 250ms 99th percentile in canary cluster
Per-tenant surge ledger entries created and summarized every 60s with <1s summarizer lag in prod-like load
Billing pipeline emits itemized surge usage line-items and reconciles to tenant credits in test invoices
Soft-tier failover triggers only when primary family capacity is insufficient and tenant opt-in flag is enabled
Console shows tenant-level surge balance, projected overage, and a history table with links to per-window allocation traces
Operator controls (pause, force-drain, disable-failover) are available and audited in the admin log
progress_updates: 2025-02-21: Kickoff sync with infra, billing, and console teams. Agreed on 250ms decision window and 60s summarization cadence.
2025-02-25: Prototype allocator implemented (Go) with token-bucket scoring. Local benchmarks show sub-10ms decisions under synthetic load.
2025-03-01: Billing changes scoped: add surge_ledger table and summarizer lambda. Mock invoice produced in staging for validation.
2025-03-04: Router integration spike completed; added metadata headers for downgrade events. Design doc updated with failure modes and telemetry.
2025-03-05: Started end-to-end dry-run in shadow mode for two pilot tenants (no billing impact). Observability dashboards created in Grafana.
comments: PM review (Rhea Martinez) 2025-02-22: Please ensure the API surface clearly separates 'request temporary burst' vs 'implicit best-effort overflow' to avoid billing confusion.
Security (Jamal Nguyen) 2025-02-24: For tenants with compliance requirements, soft-tier failover must be off by default; add an account-level flag and an approval flow for enabling it.
Design (Maya Chen) 2025-02-27: Console should offer an 'explain allocation' button that links to per-window trace and scoring details (QPS, credit balance). Keep the UI simple for non-technical PMs.
Engineer note (Liam O'Connor) 2025-03-03: Need a co-ordination window when adding surge_ledger schema change; will propose a safe migration with backfilling logic.
operator_playbook: If surge allocator returns >20% allocation failures for a pool, open incident and set pool to conservative mode (limit=50% of normal)
To temporarily pause burst for a tenant: use admin console 'Pause Burst' and notify tenant via template email
On suspected billing mismatch: run summarizer in dry-run for affected windows and compare ledger vs. invoice line-items
Emergency disable for soft-tier failover: flip per-tenant flag and force router drain of downgraded sessions
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (shadow mode): 2 pilot tenants, no billing, collect telemetry for 2 weeks
Phase 2 (dry-run billing): emit invoices with zero charge for pilot tenants; get finance sign-off
Phase 3 (opt-in beta): enable billing for pilot tenants and 5 early adopters with manual review
Phase 4 (general availability): gradual ramp to 100% of Dedicated fleet with monitoring and automatic rollback windows
